name: Lateral Inhibition
description: Suppression of neural responses by activity in neighboring neurons. A foundational computation for contrast enhancement and boundary detection. Discovered in the Limulus lateral eye and observed across all sensory systems.
computational_signature: y_i = x_i - w * sum(x_j) for j in neighborhood
key_references: Hartline, H. K., & Ratliff, F. (1957). Inhibitory interaction of receptor units in the eye of Limulus. Journal of General Physiology, 40(3), 357-376.
Carandini, M., & Heeger, D. J. (2012). Normalization as a canonical neural computation. Nature Reviews Neuroscience, 13(1), 51-62.
empirical_evidence: Directly observed in Limulus retina using intracellular recording. Extensive evidence in vertebrate retina, visual cortex (V1), and auditory brainstem. Mathematical characterization via difference-of-Gaussians and DoG-like receptive fields.
